# W2 stage S2: the epoch lockstep skeleton (walk semantics 3)

Date 2026-09-28. Branch `fable_5_1-v3-epoch` (from `fable_5_1` @ 7d25e5d2), worktree
`.claude/worktrees/fable51-epoch`. Specification: `docs/research/fable51_w2_epoch_protocol_2026-09-28.md`
(W2.0 protocol, revision 2; "the protocol" below), stage S2 of §17.2. Owner rules in force: no campaign
touched, every run <= 1 h, no computer-algebra code (Symbolica vendored plus the heap-pow working-tree patch,
unchanged; `git -C vendor/symbolica diff | sha256sum` = `629752e7...e6a4`), legacy Ordered/Ready/CP5 byte
identical.

Labels: **[M]** measured (run directory named), **[E]** estimate or interpretation, **[src]** read in source.
Nothing here is an ETA or a closure claim; `family_closure_claim` stays false. Throughput numbers are
indications only: Lockstep S2 is the deterministic control engine, not the performance engine, and the host
was loaded (load average 270-290 of 384 during the runs).

---

## 0. Summary

1. **Built** (§1): publication policy `epoch` with walk semantics 3 (probe `per_policy {ordered: 1, ready: 1,
   epoch: 3}`); module `walking/epoch/` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`); `EpochState` over an append-only
   `CompactDomain` arena, a 4,096-shard exact index with overflow, ledger6 with its exhaustive transition
   table, node flags, live bits, the edge run log with edge and records digests, and the anchor map with all
   three kinds (InitialDBand, G2Native, G2Residual); the `verify` chokepoint with private-constructor
   `Verified` tokens; byte-serialized jobs and results; Lockstep depth 1 with a serial merge P1/P2/P3
   (whole-inspection commit, IDs in (first parent, ordinal) order, antichain, full reverse retirement with
   T3/T10 transfers re-verified in P2, sorted and deduplicated edge runs before `finish`, F8 seals); result
   classes C0-C5 with the frontier-stop, error-stop and exhausted-stop policies; canonical min-ID in-merge
   resolution for controls. The closure oracle (`walk-verify-closure`) and the Python audit gained epoch
   support (independent of the engine code).
2. **Gates** (§3):

   | Gate | Verdict | Evidence [M] |
   |---|---|---|
   | (1) audit + verify-closure (full F10) on FG, BMW, H, X, four-all, four-all-p5, C-5F | **PASS** (7/7) | verify PASS with `roots_independently_verified == roots_total` (248/248, 268/268, 628/628, 656/656, 32/32, 32/32, 1/1), `assert_oracle_pass` GATE-PASS, paired audit PASS; 0 uncovered admits |
   | (2) byte identity across widths | **PASS** | W6 = W12 = W24 on the six four-loop controls; four-all and four-all-p5 also W6 = W96; C-5F W12 = W24 = W50 |
   | (3) natives, domains, edges vs legacy Ready | reported; > 5 % explained | per-family and C-5F within 5 %; four-all/p5 domains -25 % (antichain folds misses before IDs), natives +22-25 % vs Ready but -0.9 % vs Ordered |
   | (4) legacy Ordered strict identity vs 4a17f9c7 | **PASS** | FG, BMW, H, X, C-5F (and four-all, four-all-p5): 0 differing records, equal `containment_checks` |
   | (5) lib suite, `cli_routed_campaign`, Python suite, fmt | see §3.5 | license required (`RUSTRED_TESTS_REQUIRE_LICENSE=1`) |

3. **Finding: lockstep breadth enters the four-all flood** (§4). With the protocol's B = 64 the combined
   four-loop controls `four-all` and `four-all-p5` do not drain: they fall into the documented rank-13
   (anchor + 1) flood on owner `0111110010` (1.18 M rank-13 Apply IDs, 3.38 M natives when stopped at
   1,253 s), the same non-drain signature as 6 of 13 legacy Ready W96 runs. A B scan (diagnostic seam
   `RUSTRED_EPOCH_LOCKSTEP_B`) drains at B = 1, 4, 8, 16, 24 (four-all 29,811-29,892 natives; p5 31,452-31,453)
   and floods at B = 32 and 64. S2 therefore ships **B = 16** (deviation D1). The per-family controls FG, BMW,
   H and X drain and pass the oracle gate at both B = 64 and B = 16. The rolling production schedule (S6, W96) will face the same breadth effect; it is an input
   property made visible by wide fronts, not an engine soundness issue (every drained run is certified).

| Dispatch (§8.3) | `E/dispatch.rs` | requeued IDs first (attempts < 2, at most half the refill while Pending exists), a deferred share, then a monotone cursor over Pending; T2 at enqueue; `Drained` / `Stalled` (C5) |
| Merge P1 (§6.2, §9.1) | `E/merge.rs::p1_check`, `classify` | in-flight seq and v0, Reserved, classes C0-C4 and C5, event parity per class, InitialDBand re-validation (R1/R2 plus the D >= cut slice verified inside the anchor), aggregate event/frontier allowances |
| Merge P2 (§6.3; serial in S2) | `E/merge.rs::p2_plan` | F1 digest recomputed from every shipped image; canonical resolution (exact, dominant orthant, minimum live ID of the index; the winner verified); order-independent antichain per bucket (pairwise, or through a temporary kernel index above 64 candidates, tested equal); provisional order (first parent position, ordinal); reverse sets with a `Planned` token per old ID (smallest containing survivor position) |
| Merge P3 (§6.4) | `E/merge.rs::p3_preflight`, `p3_apply` | preflight of every per-ID arena, exact shards, edge log, anchors and the record sink, the ID cap (F9) and the u48 epoch (F13); apply: IDs, index maintenance and live bits (checked retired count), T3/T10 transfers with their alias runs and seals, results in cut order with sorted deduplicated runs, T4/T5/T6, F8 seals, records, requeue T7/T8, advance k |

## 2. The oracles for semantics 3

- **walk-verify-closure.** `epoch_export.rs` reads the export without engine code: lengths and blake3 of every
  file against the manifest, the canonical images through the shared compact encoding, the run log expanded to
  pairs, ledger6 decoded by its own reader. The verifier's ordinary path then runs unchanged (records to nodes,
  F8 on records against the saved seal flags, alias containment, partial-record anchor rules and exact union
  cover, closure re-derived from the edges, full F10 re-inspection with every lever off, the result binding).
  Epoch-only re-derivations: valid ledger6 tags and per-tag counts, the F8 seal rule on the saved flags,
  ledger6 tag vs record kind (Native / NativeFrontier / NativeError), forward same-bucket aliases with exactly
  their one-edge run and no alias below P0, one run per merged native with strictly increasing targets below
  W, merge epochs <= k, the edge digest and the records digest `(id, tag, out-degree)` recomputed from the runs
  (the out-degree check of master plan §6 check 5), and the InitialDBand anchor rules. The request binding is
  `epoch_request_binding` (A7: workers, schedule and aggregate allowances are not bound).
- **Negative controls on an epoch export** [M, `TMP/epoch-s2/runs/mutations/`, FG W6]: `dropped-edge`
  FAIL (successor_uncovered), `retargeted-alias` FAIL (alias_containment + epoch_alias), `seal-with-frontier`
  FAIL (seal parity, false closure, epoch_ledger, ...), `injected-false-hit` FAIL, `miscounted-events` FAIL,
  `retargeted-anchor` FAIL (partial_anchor, partial_union_cover), `alias-chain-detour` PASS (the positive
  control); `hidden-frontier` not applicable (FG has no frontier). A one-byte flip in `ledger6-1.bin` is
  refused at load ("epoch export checksum or length mismatch").
- **Audit.** Policy `epoch` accepted: records in merge order with `accepted_events` on every native (as
  Ready), the pool's `merged_inspections` must equal the native records and `returned = merged + discarded`,
  and `--checkpoint` must hold `epoch-export.json` whose metadata equals the result's checkpoint object. A
  Python test covers the pass case and three violations.

The final binary `rustred-da364dc6` (the gate binary plus lint cleanup) reproduces `s2b-w6/fg` and

Identity is by construction: a lockstep epoch dispatches the same B IDs whatever the width, every resolver
input of S2 is the job's own domain, and the merge is a function of the sorted cut and the state.

### 3.3 Gate (3): natives, domains, edges vs legacy Ready [M]

Epoch `s2b-w6` against legacy 4a17f9c7 Ready W6 (`ref-ready-w6`, same CPUs 2-7, one run each: Ready is
schedule-dependent) and, for context, the Ordered W6 references of the integrator (`TMP/fable51-controls/
int-ref-g3`). Domains = scheduled IDs; edges = the closure monitor's dependency edges (`descendant_closure.
dependency_edges`, deduplicated per source, alias and anchor edges included). Table `TMP/epoch-s2/gate3-w6.json`.

| Control | Natives E / Ready / Ordered | E vs Ready | Domains E / Ready / Ordered | E vs Ready | Edges E / Ready / Ordered | E vs Ready |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| FG | 98,748 / 98,846 / 98,869 | -0.10 % | 98,840 / 98,886 / 98,909 | -0.05 % | 540,111 / 540,354 / 540,397 | -0.04 % |
| BMW | 143,516 / 148,319 / 147,233 | -3.24 % | 154,413 / 159,148 / 158,951 | -2.98 % | 1,858,471 / 1,928,362 / 1,915,548 | -3.62 % |
| H | 24,497 / 24,777 / 24,680 | -1.13 % | 24,761 / 24,959 / 24,929 | -0.79 % | 109,706 / 110,405 / 110,275 | -0.63 % |
| X | 46,602 / 46,826 / 46,826 | -0.48 % | 46,979 / 47,211 / 47,193 | -0.49 % | 259,231 / 260,589 / 260,571 | -0.52 % |
| four-all | 29,892 / 24,502 / 30,159 | **+22.0 %** | 48,834 / 65,546 / 65,444 | **-25.5 %** | 1,191,450 / 1,126,846 / 1,239,515 | **+5.7 %** |
| four-all-p5 | 31,453 / 25,109 / 31,717 | **+25.3 %** | 51,545 / 68,545 / 68,483 | **-24.8 %** | 1,268,542 / 1,189,503 / 1,315,404 | **+6.6 %** |
| C-5F (epoch W24; legacy W16) | 960,538 / 981,188 / 967,621 | -2.10 % | 1,215,537 / 1,276,360 / 1,273,376 | -4.77 % | 12,314,557 / 12,663,703 / 12,518,693 | -2.76 % |

C-5F legacy Ready: 4a17f9c7 W16 on CPUs 0-7,256-263 (`ref-ready-w16`); Ordered: `int-ref-g3/five-finite` (W16).

Differences above 5 % (bold), explained:
- **four-all / four-all-p5 domains -25 %** against both legacy policies: the legacy lanes admit every miss at
  once and later transfer it when a containing successor arrives (35,285 / 41,044 alias records); the epoch
  merge folds the non-maximal misses of a cut into their containing survivor before any ID exists (P2
  antichain: 18,942 aliases). The same effect is 0.05-3 % on the per-family controls, whose successors are
  rarely contained in a sibling's.
- **four-all / four-all-p5 natives +22-25 % vs Ready, -0.9 % vs Ordered**: legacy Ready inspects fewer natives
  on these controls than Ordered in every run (W6: 24,482-26,065 in five runs; README section 5); the
  deterministic lockstep FIFO behaves like Ordered (30,159 / 31,717). The Ready-vs-Ordered gap is a legacy
  scheduling effect (Ready commits results as they finish, so containers arrive before later dispatches),
  not an epoch effect.
- **four-all / four-all-p5 edges +5.7-6.6 % vs Ready, -3.6 to -3.9 % vs Ordered**: edges follow natives
  (+22-25 %); per native the epoch has fewer edges than Ready.

## 4. Lockstep breadth and the four-all flood

**Measured [M]** (binary `rustred-0277a7f9`, identical engine to the gate binary except the default B; seam
`RUSTRED_EPOCH_LOCKSTEP_B`; runs `TMP/epoch-s2/runs/bexp-*`, W2-W6 on CPUs 0-15,256-271):

| B | four-all | four-all-p5 |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | drained, 29,889 natives | - |
| 4 | drained, 29,890 | - |
| 8 | drained, 29,892 | drained, 31,452 |
| 16 | drained, 29,892 (the gate binary: 29,892) | drained, 31,453 |
| 24 | drained, 29,811 | - |
| 32 | flood: 129,216 natives at 40 s (stopped) | - |
| 64 | flood: 3.38 M natives, 5.64 M IDs at 1,253 s (stopped; `s2a-w6/four-all`) | flood: 1.52 M natives at 295 s (stopped; `s2a-w6/four-all-p5`) |

Reference: Ordered 4a17f9c7 30,159 (four-all) and 31,717 (p5); gate C-4L-comb-O: drained, 0 frontiers, oracle
PASS, natives <= 33,175 (orchestrator decision 5). The drained B = 16 run has 29 rank-13 Apply natives on
`0111110010` (drained legacy runs: 30; README section 5), 7,811 IDs of rank >= 13 in all.

**Signature of the B = 64 non-drain** [M, `TMP/epoch-s2/runs/s2a-w6/four-all/checkpoint`]: 1,176,650 rank-13
Apply IDs on `0111110010` (anchor rank 12 + 1), then its Route descendants (`0111010010`, `0101110010`,
`0111100000`, ...), point-like on lines 1-2 with an unbounded dot on line 3: the "fragmenting mode" of README
section 5, identical to the legacy Ready W96 non-drains. Up to the rank-13 layer the epoch walk explores the
same domains in the same relative order as Ordered (of the first 1,000 epoch IDs, 996 exist in the Ordered
reference, mapped monotonically: epoch 50 -> Ordered 1,917, 517 -> 15,623, 21,026 -> 44,039); the first
epoch-only domain on the flood's path is a rank-13 Route domain on `0101111001` (epoch ID 15,543) that the
Ordered walk never creates. The near-orthant rank-13 container of Ordered (44,039) also exists in the epoch
walk (21,026, later transferred to a larger container).

**Interpretation [E].** B is the number of IDs reserved at once. Reserved IDs never transfer (S3), so a wide
front inspects domains that a narrow front would have transferred to the containers created by its
predecessors; on `four-all` that is enough to seed the self-sustaining rank-13 layer, exactly as the 96
in-flight inspections of legacy Ready W96 do in 6 of 13 runs. Ordered (dispatch fence 256, but containers
admitted after every single native) behaves like a narrow front. This is an input property (the rank-12
anchors leave rank 13 uncovered on a flooding owner) that the schedule exposes; it is not an engine soundness
issue (each drained run is independently certified) and not a determinism issue (every B is identical across
widths).

**Consequences.**
- S2 ships B = 16 (deviation D1): all four-loop and five-loop controls drain; the lockstep front caps useful
  inspection parallelism at 16, which is acceptable for the control engine.
- The rolling production schedule (S6, W96, and RollingLite at the owner gate) has a front of about I + D_max
  jobs. It will meet the same effect on `four-all`, which is why C-4L-comb-R is statistical against legacy
  Ready at the same widths (decision 5). The five-loop inputs have the same anchor + 1 structure
  (orchestrator decision 3a: L* rank escapes); the dispatch-order and enqueue-depth work of W3.1 and the
  frontier/rank-escape rescue of LC1 are the levers, not a smaller front.
- Lockstep depth 2 (MVP-B) doubles the reserved front at a given B; its B must be chosen with the same scan.

## 5. Deviations from the protocol (disposition style)

Legend as in protocol §20: **F** = as specified; **P** = partly adopted, with the reason; **D** = deliberate
deviation, with the reason.

| # | Protocol text | S2 | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Lockstep B = 64 (§6.1, §8.1) | **D**: B = 16 (constant, unbound; seam `RUSTRED_EPOCH_LOCKSTEP_B` for diagnostics) | B >= 32 enters the four-all/p5 rank-13 flood (§4); every B <= 24 tested drains |
| D2 | Chunk trees for every per-ID array, snapshot byte segments, frozen bits (§3.2-3.4) | **P**: plain vectors on the coordinator; no snapshot | S2 has no inspector-side lookups (S4); nothing reads state concurrently |
| D3 | No per-ID summary slab; `verify` recomputes (§0 item 15) | **P**: the reused kernel-lane index keeps its per-ID `CompactSummary` (92 B/ID) as its prefilter; `verify` itself never reads it (raw inclusion, else the native summary recomputed) | IMP-13: S2 reuses the kernel index as code; S4's layers replace it |
| D4 | `JobBytes` 128 B fixed, `ResultBytes` header 128 B, typed record bytes (§2.4) | **P**: job = 32-B header + canonical image (37 + 4N B); result = fixed LE header + length-prefixed parts; stats, frontiers and refusal provenance as JSON byte strings | typed binary records are S3 (§17.2); the boundary is byte-only either way |
| D5 | Resolution pipeline tiers 0-7 on the inspector (§5.2) | **P**: tier 0 (F1 image, summary) and tier 1 (job-local exact set) on the inspector; every other request resolved in the merge | task: "no inspector-side lookups yet (S4)"; the protocol prescribes in-merge resolution for S2 |
| D6 | Canonical mode = minimum ID over all verified stored containers (§5.2) | **P**: exact image, else the bucket's dominant full orthant, else the minimum *live* ID of the ID-ordered index; the winner verified | the S2 wording "canonical in-merge resolution over the kernel lane's ID-ordered SoA index" and v3 S2 "through `Queue::admit` (minimum ID)": the legacy index semantics; deterministic in the store |
| D7 | Antichain via the SoA kernel above 64 misses (§6.3 step 4) | **F**: a temporary kernel index above 64 candidates, pairwise below; tested equal (`antichain_indexed_equals_pairwise`) | - |
| D8 | P3 infallible after the preflight (§6.4) | **P**: every arena preflighted; the kernel index's `prepare` runs inside apply (its tail-block reservation depends on the insertions before it) and a failure there is C5 (no save exists in S2, so nothing half-applied can persist) | the reused index API reserves per insertion |
| D9 | P4 layers and publish (§6.5) | **P**: no P4; the index is maintained in P3 (IMP-13) | S4 |
| D10 | Canary (§6.6), poison stickiness | **P**: no canary (no inspector hits exist in S2: every edge target is a P2 token); a C5 writes `poison-<k>.json` into the export directory; restore-side stickiness is S3 | nothing to sample |
| D11 | Stop paths, CP6, crash journal, guard, isolation (§8.4, §11) | **P**: cooperative stop cancels in-flight natives (C1, requeued, no penalty) and ends with status `stopped`, exit 4, no save; attempts/last_err counters and the deferred share are live; guard, isolation and the journal are S3 | task: no checkpoints yet (S3) |
| D12 | `--checkpoint` is CP6 | **D**: in S2, `--checkpoint DIR` names a final non-resumable export (manifest `epoch-export.json`) read by the oracles; `--resume` refused | the verifier and the audit need the state; CP6 replaces it in S3 |
| D13 | Break reasons none/allowance/resolver_range/resolver_summary/spill_io/alloc/cancel | **P**: adds `resolver_diagnostic` (a third optional-refusal provenance record or an unserializable frontier: C2) and `protocol` (an impossible event: C5) | explicit classes for two resolver refusals |
| D14 | Stop reasons (§9.2) | **P**: adds `frontier_allowance` (aggregate `max_frontiers` under `record`) | the aggregate allowance still exists in the request |
| D15 | P0 = protected initial prefix | **F**, always (not only with D-bands) | R1 needs it for every epoch walk; all controls use D-bands anyway |
| D16 | Refresh (A6), MergedView built, G2' planner | **P**: A6 off (Lockstep); `MergedView` type and visibility rule only; G2' planner W4 | as §7 "In W2 only MergedView ... land" |
| D17 | Tests of §17.2 S2 | **P**: 17 unit tests + 3 fixture e2e tests (see §3.5); not built: `p3_preflight_failure_is_noop` injected at every reserve (a capacity no-op is tested), `p1_initial_d_band_revalidation` as a unit test (exercised on FG: 104 partial records), `termination_requires_monitor_available`, `s2_closure_forced_refresh_only`, `p3_per_native_cost` (P3 wall is reported per run instead), `local_final_verified_in_p2` and `dispatch_cursor_restore_min_pending` (no Locals, no restore in S2) | time |
| D18 | Epoch scheduling policy | **D**: epoch requires `TransferUnreserved` (its lookahead is unused and unbound) | transfers are part of semantics 3; keeps the control argv unchanged |

C-5F: epoch W24 690 s traversal against legacy Ordered W16 254 s (integrator, `int-ref-g3`) and legacy Ready W16 213 s (`ref-ready-w16`).

Reading [E]: S2 is as fast as the legacy lanes on the small controls and 2-3x slower on C-5F, as expected of a
lockstep front of 16 that waits for the slowest native of each epoch (77 % of C-5F traversal) with a serial
P2 on the coordinator (18 %). Wider widths do not help S2 (W24 = W6). Per native, P3 costs 16-27 us here
(it builds and streams the JSON record, maintains the kernel index and the Tracker); the protocol's
<= 10 us budget is an S4 gate on typed records with P4 helpers. None of these numbers bears on the owner
gate (S4 RollingLite against the legacy + SoA comparator).

## 7. What S3 and S4 need next

**S3 (CP6, stops, journal)**: replace the S2 export by CP6 generations (the export's sections are already
the §11.7 layouts for ledger6, nodes, edges and anchors, each digest-bound); `MergeBoundary` after P3 and the
bookkeeping-only merge for stops (S2's discard path `merge::discard_cut` is its seed); typed binary records
with the P3 trailer (the JSON view is in `E/records.rs`); the inflight journal, guard derivation, isolation
and `--exhaust-id` / `--retry-exhausted` (ledger6 already carries the counters and T8/T9/T12); poison
stickiness at restore; the restore validators (the verifier's `epoch_export::check` is an independent model of
them); the stop-file contract. The verifier's epoch reader must learn the CP6 manifest.

**S4 (inspector resolution)**: the snapshot (`Arc<Box<..>>` byte segments, frozen bits, MergedView) and tiers
2-7 on the inspector (self-scope, Local through `Container::JobMiss`, MRU, orthants/hints, pattern and young
tiers) with the canary; replace the reused kernel-lane index and its per-ID summaries (D3) by the layers; the
delta check of P2 against entries newer than v0 (not needed in S2, where v0 = k); per-CCX replicas; P2 on
helpers. Two S2 results constrain S4 and S6:
- the lockstep/rolling front width changes the walk on `four-all` (§4): S4's owner gate runs RollingLite at
  W >= 24, and its soundness preconditions include C-4L-comb-O/-R; expect the same breadth effect there;
- S2's coordinator is dominated by waiting for the slowest native of each lockstep epoch (C-5F: 531 s of
  690 s traversal) and by serial P2 lookups (126 s): Rolling and helper-parallel P2 are the levers.

**Open items from S2**: the per-family and C-5F natives are 0.1-3 % below legacy Ordered (fewer IDs: the cut's
antichain folds non-maximal misses before ID assignment); `four-all` domains are 25 % below both legacy
policies for the same reason (aliases -46 to -54 %).

## 8. Reproduction

- Build: `TMP/epoch-s2/cargo.sh` (worktree; `flock build-3.lock`, CPUs 0-15,256-271, `nix develop --command cargo
  ... --release --locked --offline`, `RUSTRED_TESTS_REQUIRE_LICENSE=1`). Binaries with sha256 prefixes in
  `TMP/epoch-s2/bin/` (main tree TMP): `rustred-142a3ae6` gate binary (B = 16), `rustred-0277a7f9` (B = 64
  default plus the seam), `rustred-760f85ec` / `rustred-d015999d` earlier (B = 64).
- Controls: `TMP/epoch-s2/run_control.py` (shared runner, lane output root `TMP/epoch-s2/runs`),
  `TMP/epoch-s2/controls.sh BIN LABEL W CPUS "FAMILIES" [oracle]`, `TMP/epoch-s2/matrix.sh`,
  `TMP/epoch-s2/socket1_session.sh` (socket1.lock). Oracle: `TMP/epoch-s2/oracle.sh BIN RUNDIR CPUS THREADS`.
  Identity: `TMP/epoch-s2/identity.py RUN_A RUN_B`. Gate 3: `TMP/epoch-s2/compare.py EPOCH_LABEL READY_LABEL`.
  Gate 4: `TMP/epoch-s2/ordered_identity.sh NEWBIN LABEL`.
- An epoch control argv is the historical one with `--publication-policy epoch`; `--checkpoint DIR` must name a
  new directory (the S2 export).
